faq.heading: Frequently Asked Questions
faq.subtitle: Short answers about the new Nostr-only Obelisk.

q1.question: What is Obelisk?
q1.answer: Obelisk is an open-source, Discord-style group chat client that runs entirely on Nostr. There is no backend and no database: every message is a signed Nostr event published directly to the relays you choose. Groups are NIP-29 groups, DMs are encrypted Nostr DMs, and your account is a Nostr keypair.

q2.question: Is there a server I have to sign up to?
q2.answer: No. Obelisk is a frontend. There is no signup, no email, no password, and no Obelisk account. You log in with a Nostr key and the app talks straight to your configured relays: there is no Obelisk application backend or database. Messages live on relays. Obelisk operates two public relays; every other relay is controlled by its own operator.

q3.question: What relays does Obelisk use?
q3.answer: Whatever relays you tell it to. New installs currently include wss://public.obelisk.ar and wss://lacrypta-relay.obelisk.ar, both operated by Obelisk. You can add, remove, or replace relays from the relay rail. Every other relay is independent and controlled by its own operator.

q4.question: Do I need an email or phone number?
q4.answer: No. Obelisk has no signup form. You log in with a Nostr key, via a browser extension (NIP-07) or by pasting an nsec. NIP-46 bunker support is on the roadmap.

q5.question: How are groups implemented?
q5.answer: Obelisk uses NIP-29: relay-managed groups. Channels, members, admins, kicks and bans are all standard NIP-29 events that the relay enforces. Any NIP-29-compatible relay works. You can host your own relay, run a private one for your community, or use a public one.

q6.question: Are my messages encrypted?
q6.answer: Direct messages are end-to-end encrypted. Obelisk sends NIP-17 gift-wrapped messages by default, so relays cannot see who you are talking to, and you can switch a conversation back to NIP-04 if the other person's client needs it. Turn on post-quantum protection in settings and the message is sealed with a post-quantum envelope as well, whenever your signer and the other person both have post-quantum keys. Group messages are signed but public on the relay: anyone the relay lets in can read them, just like a Discord channel. Run a private relay if you need a closed group.

q7.question: Can I self-host Obelisk?
q7.answer: Yes, Obelisk is a Next.js app and 'hosting' it just means serving static-style HTML/JS. There's no database to manage and no backend service to run. Run it locally with `npm run dev`, ship it to any Node host, or expose it through a tunnel. We're working on a static-export build for one-click deployment to GitHub Pages, S3, or any static CDN.

q8.question: How do I get a Nostr key?
q8.answer: You can generate one in the login screen. If you want a standalone signer, install a NIP-07 browser extension like Alby or nos2x, or on mobile use Amber (Android) or nsec.app. Keep your nsec safe: it's your account, no one can recover it for you.

q9.question: What about voice channels?
q9.answer: Voice is on the roadmap. The previous voice implementation used a Socket.io signaling server, which doesn't fit a backend-free architecture: we're rebuilding it as P2P WebRTC with relay-based signaling so it stays pure Nostr.

q10.question: Does Obelisk work on mobile?
q10.answer: Yes. Obelisk is a responsive web app and works in any modern mobile browser. Pair it with a NIP-07-compatible signer (or a NIP-46 bunker, once shipped) for a smooth login. A dedicated PWA build is on the roadmap.

features.heading: Why Obelisk
features.subtitle: All the chat. None of the servers. Your keys, your relays, signed events.

nostrIdentity.title: Nostr login: your keys, your account
nostrIdentity.desc: Sign in with NIP-07 or your nsec. There is no Obelisk account to create. Your Nostr key is the account, everywhere.

realtimeChat.title: NIP-29 groups
realtimeChat.desc: Channels, members, admins, kicks and bans are all standard NIP-29 events on the relay. Open protocol, no proprietary format, no lock-in.

encryptedDMs.title: Encrypted DMs
encryptedDMs.desc: Direct messages are end-to-end encrypted Nostr DMs, gift-wrapped with NIP-17 by default and NIP-04 when a conversation needs it. Only you and the recipient can read them.

voice.title: P2P voice channels over Nostr
voice.desc: Talk to anyone in a channel with no media server in the middle. Voice is WebRTC peer-to-peer; signaling rides on Nostr events, just like every other message.

selfHosted.title: No backend, no database
selfHosted.desc: Obelisk is a frontend. There is no Postgres, no Socket.io server, no auth service. Every message is a signed event sent straight to a relay.

spamResistant.title: Static-site self-hosting
spamResistant.desc: Self-hosting means serving HTML and JS. No database to operate, no Docker required. Run it from your laptop, a tunnel, or a static host.

zaps.title: Bitcoin zaps in chat
zaps.desc: Send sats from any message via NIP-57 zaps and Nostr Wallet Connect (NIP-47). No custodian, no platform fee, no middleman.

games.title: Games on the relay
games.desc: Chain Reaction, Vesta and Stacker run inside a channel with no game server. Every move is a signed event, and every client replays the same log to the same board.

adminCli.title: Open source
adminCli.desc: MIT-licensed, every line on GitHub. Read it, fork it, audit it, run it. The whole app is the client you can see.

sfu.description: Large rooms switch to a mediasoup SFU advertised by the channel. Choose which SFU server to use or host your own. Media remains DTLS-SRTP transport encrypted while avoiding a full mesh between every participant.

pqc.heading: Post-quantum messages
pqc.subtitle: Encrypted messages sent today can be recorded now and read years from now, once a quantum computer breaks the key exchange Nostr relies on. It is the one part of the problem that can be fixed in advance.
pqc.status: Live in Obelisk. Direct messages are gift-wrapped by default, and carry a post-quantum seal once you turn post-quantum protection on and your signer and the other person both have post-quantum keys. The keys themselves live in the Nostr WoT extension and the @nostr-wot/pq library.

nostrwot.desc: Identity, signer and post-quantum keys derived from a single 24-word recovery phrase.

quantakrypto.desc: Applied post-quantum cryptography: design, specification and cryptographic review.

pqc.guide: Read the guide: making your DMs quantum-safe
